name: Pupil Light Reflex
description: Analyzes pupillary light reflex timing and magnitude — AI-generated faces lack proper pupil constriction responses.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated or deepfake video by analyzing whether the pupils exhibit physiologically correct light reflex responses:

1. **Pupil Segmentation and Tracking**: The method segments the pupil in each eye using a combination of iris detection (Daugman's integrodifferential operator) and pupil boundary estimation. The iris is first localized using circular Hough transform, then the pupil boundary is refined using active contour (snake) models that track the dark-to-light transition at the pupil-iris border. Pupil diameter is measured in each frame with sub-pixel accuracy (~0.1 pixel precision). Both left and right pupils are tracked independently. The method handles partial occlusion from eyelids by fitting ellipses rather than circles when the pupil is partially covered.

2. **Pupillary Light Reflex (PLR) Dynamics**: In authentic video, pupils constrict in response to light increases and dilate in response to light decreases. The PLR follows well-characterized dynamics: (a) latency — constriction begins 200–300 ms after light onset, (b) constriction velocity — peak velocity of 3–6 mm/s, (c) maximum constriction — pupils can constrict to ~2 mm diameter from a resting ~4–5 mm, (d) redilation — after maximum constriction, the pupil partially redilates (pupillary escape) with time constant ~1.5 seconds. The method estimates scene illumination changes from the video (using average luminance in the face region) and checks whether pupil diameter changes follow the expected PLR transfer function. AI-generated faces typically show either static pupils (no PLR at all) or incorrect timing and magnitude of pupillary responses.

3. **Consensual Pupillary Response**: A critical physiological constraint is that both pupils must respond simultaneously to light changes — light entering one eye causes constriction in both eyes (consensual response, mediated by bilateral innervation via the Edinger-Westphal nucleus). The method measures the cross-correlation between left and right pupil diameter time series. In authentic video, the correlation coefficient exceeds 0.95 with zero lag. AI-generated faces often show: (a) uncorrelated pupil sizes — left and right pupils change independently, (b) asymmetric baseline — one pupil is consistently larger than the other beyond the normal 0.4 mm physiological anisocoria, (c) temporal desynchronization — one pupil responds before the other.

4. **Hippus and Spontaneous Pupillary Oscillations**: Even under constant illumination, real pupils exhibit spontaneous oscillations called hippus — rhythmic pupillary fluctuations at 0.5–2 Hz with amplitude of 0.2–0.5 mm. These oscillations reflect autonomic nervous system activity and are correlated between the two eyes. The method analyzes the power spectral density of pupil diameter time series and checks for: (a) presence of hippus oscillations in the 0.5–2 Hz band, (b) bilateral coherence of oscillations, (c) absence of non-physiological high-frequency fluctuations (> 5 Hz) that would indicate per-frame rendering noise. AI-generated pupils typically lack hippus entirely (perfectly stable diameter) or show high-frequency noise inconsistent with neurological control.
parameters:
Pupil detection: Daugman integrodifferential + active contour
Diameter measurement precision: ~0.1 pixels
PLR latency: 200–300 ms expected
PLR constriction velocity: 3–6 mm/s
Maximum constriction: ~2 mm diameter
Redilation time constant: ~1.5 seconds
Consensual response correlation: > 0.95
Physiological anisocoria: < 0.4 mm
Hippus frequency band: 0.5–2 Hz
Hippus amplitude: 0.2–0.5 mm
Minimum eye resolution: 40×40 pixels
accuracy: 80–90% accuracy detecting AI-generated faces via pupillary reflex analysis. PLR dynamics consistency achieves AUC of 0.87. Consensual response analysis provides F1-score of 0.89. Hippus detection adds 3–5% improvement. Performance requires sufficient eye resolution and visible illumination changes in the scene.
source: Guo, Y. et al. (2022). Eyes Tell All: Detecting Political Orientation from Eye Movement Data. PNAS, 119(29), e2112552119.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated face video through pupillary physiology violations. Forensic analysis of testimony video authenticity. Deepfake detection in scenarios with varying illumination. Biometric liveness detection for security applications.
strengths:
• Based on well-characterized neurological reflexes with precise timing constraints
• Consensual response provides bilateral consistency check
• Hippus analysis detects absence of autonomic nervous system signatures
• Works independently of face identity, expression, or pose
• Difficult for generators to simulate without explicit pupillary physiology models
limitations:
• Requires sufficient eye resolution (at least 40×40 pixels per eye)
• Constant illumination scenes provide less PLR signal to analyze
• Colored contact lenses or dark irises may reduce pupil measurement accuracy
• Drug effects (mydriatics, miotics) alter normal PLR parameters
• Some advanced generators may implement basic pupil size modulation
